newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LOME MEMBERSHIP WILL STRENGHTEN S.AFRICA/EU TIES.
newsitem.headline: LOME MEMBERSHIP WILL STRENGHTEN S.AFRICA/EU TIES.

text.p: South Africa's political and economic ties with the European Union and Africa will be strengthened by its qualified membership of the Lome Convention, EU ambassador Erwan Fouere said on Thursday.
South Africa was due to sign an accession protocol later on Thursday in Luxembourg, making it the 71st member of Lome.

"The qualified membership of South Africa to Lome is a very important decision and marks a further milestone in the strengthening of relations between South Africa, the African continent and the European Union," Fouere told businessmen.
The Lome Convention is a cooperation agreement between the 15 EU members and 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries.

Fouere said the political consequences of South Africa joining Lome were that it would strengthen the ACP countries' bargaining position in renegotiating the Convention which expires at the end of 1999.

"South Africa's involvement in the Lome renegotiation is of crucial importance, and South Africa will also take part in political dialogue between the EU and the Lome Convention which has up to now not given the dividends which one would have wished."
He said the focus of that dialogue was to look at preventative diplomacy and conflict resolution mechanisms to deal with problems on the African continent before they happened.

Although it would not be eligible for non-reciprocal trade preferences, South Africa would now be eligible to tender for lucrative European Development Fund contracts worth up to 45 billion rand, Fouere said.
Fouere said bilateral negotiations between the EU and South Africa, which were focusing on issues not covered by South Africa's qualified Lome membership, were continuing albeit slowly.
"The decision taken this week will add a significant and psychological boost to the momentum which has been initiated."

He said the reason for the negotiations proceeding slowly was because South Africa was dealing with the priorities and pressures from its regional neighbours who had to benefit from any agreement reached with the EU.
Fouere said trade talks with the EU aimed at eventually setting up a free trade agreement will have to be speeded up to lure foreign investors.

He said the next round of talks scheduled for May would focus on the economic aspects of a bilateral relationship and in June talks would focus on the dismantlement of specific trade and tariff barriers.

"Above all it is essential keep the momentum of these negotiations going because the business community requires a clear message of what will be the overall framework between South Africa and its largest trading partner, the EU," he said.
